1.why: auth() derives identity solely from the bank_session cookie and rejects any session whose userId is not the account, while suppliedIdentifier() rejects client-supplied user IDs, so MFA endpoints only ever touch the signed-in owner's settings.

2.why: Verification codes are TOTP values bound to the session owner's pending secret and marked used on success; no other user context exists in which the same code could be redeemed.

3.why: /api/mfa/verify sets account.enabled without invalidating or rotating any sessions, so the enabling session and any other concurrent sessions continue to work after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The pending secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted via encrypt(), account.secret retains that ciphertext, and recovery codes are stored as SHA-256 hash plus AES-GCM ciphertext, never plaintext.

5.why: token(), base32() secret generation, and recoveryCode() all use crypto.getRandomValues, and TOTP codes derive via HMAC-SHA1 from that CSPRNG-generated secret.

6.why: The only cookie (bank_session) is HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, and the client keeps the CSRF token and secrets only in JS variables/DOM, never in localStorage or readable cookies.

7.why: The server validates email (emailOK), phone (phoneOK), OTP (/^\d{6}$/), recovery code format, JSON content-type, and a 4KB body cap before using any input.

8.why: All client-side rendering of server values passes through esc() (textContent to innerHTML encoding), and the per-response nonce CSP blocks any injected inline script.

9.why: There are no server-side redirects and client navigation is hash routing constrained to the fixed internal views returned by needed(), so no open redirect is possible.

10.why: headers() sets a nonce-based CSP, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, and frame-ancestors 'none' on every response.

11.why: The Set-Cookie for bank_session includes HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict both when issued at login and when cleared at logout.

12.why: The client log() function writes the provisioning secret, testOtp, and all recovery codes to console and the on-page #logs panel, so seeds and codes are not kept out of logs, though server errors are generic with no stack traces.

13.why: The pending enrollment expires after OTP_LIFE (5 minutes) and is marked used on success, recovery codes are marked used on redeem, and TOTP codes are inherently time-stepped.

14.why: Five failed OTP attempts set p.locked for LOCK (10 minutes) and five failed recovery attempts set account.recoveryLocked similarly.

15.why: Login deletes the prior session and issues a fresh token, auth() enforces 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and expires the cookie.
